Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:10:1.hebrew: ורואה את קדשיו - ואינו נחשד לומר על מום עובר שהוא קבוע, דמה לו לשקר? הא אם היה רוצה להוציאן לחול — יכול לעשות בהיתר, ולישאל לחכם, ולפתוח בחרטה דהקדש טעות ולומר: "בטעות הקדשתיו". אבל בבכור, דאיהו לא אקדשיה — דהא מרחם קדוש — ליכא למימר הכי, ונחשד:
Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:10:1.english: And he may inspect his own sanctified animals - And he is not suspected of saying about a transient blemish that it is permanent, for why would he lie? For if he wanted to remove them to non-sacred status, he could do [so] permissibly, and inquire of a Sage and open with regret [on grounds] of mistaken consecration and say: “I consecrated it in error.” But regarding a firstborn, which he did not consecrate — for it is sanctified from the womb — this cannot be said, and he is [therefore] suspected.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:11:1.hebrew: ומעשרותיו - דאינו נחשד לומר על עובר שהוא קבוע, דאי הוה בעי מעיקרא, הוה עביד בהיתירא קודם שיעשר עדרו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:11:1.english: And his [animal] tithes - For he is not suspected of saying about a transient [blemish] that it is permanent, for if he had wanted [to do so] at the outset, he could have acted permissibly before he tithed his herd.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:11:2.hebrew: שדי מומא בכולהו - דעדיין אינן קדושים דליהוי כמטיל מום בקדשים, ואח"כ יעשר, דמעשר בהמה חל על המום, דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:ל״ג) לא יבקר בין טוב לרע. הילכך, אינו נחשד:
Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:11:2.english: [He can] inflict a blemish upon all of them - For they are not yet consecrated, such that it would be [considered] like inflicting a blemish upon consecrated animals; and afterward he could tithe [them], for animal tithe takes effect [even] upon [an animal with] a blemish, as it is written: (Leviticus 27:33) "He shall not inquire whether it be good or bad." Therefore, he is not suspected.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:12:1.hebrew: ונשאל על טהרותיו - אינו חשוד לומר על טמא טהור, דאם טמאות הן — מה יפסיד? הא חזא ליה בימי טומאה. ובחולין קמיירי, דתרומה טמאה לא חזיא ליה אפילו בימי טומאתו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:12:1.english: And [one] may be asked concerning his pure [items] - He is not suspected of declaring [something that is] impure to be pure, for if they are impure, what would he lose? Behold, it is fit for him in the days of [his] impurity. And [the baraita] is dealing with non-sacred food, as impure terumah is not fit for him even in the days of his impurity.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:14:1.english: All disqualified consecrated [animals] - Consecrated [animals] in which a blemish developed.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:14:2.hebrew: הנאתן להקדש - אם מוכרין אותן ביוקר, הנאת הקדש היא. ובגמרא מפרשא כולה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:14:2.english: Their benefit is to the Temple treasury - If they sell them at a high price, it is to the benefit of the Temple treasury. And in the Gemara, the entire matter is explained:

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:14:3.hebrew: באיטליז - בשוק שלוקחין הרבה, ונמכר ביוקר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:14:3.english: In the butchers' market - In a market where many [people] buy, and [the meat] is sold at a higher price.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:14:4.english: And they are weighed by the litra - In the manner that butchers sell non-sacred meat.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:15:1.english: A firstborn and a tithe - [The benefit realized] if they are sold at a high price.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:15:2.hebrew: הנאתן לבעלים - בכור, הנאתו לכהן, ומוכר הבשר לכל מי שירצה, דבשר בכור נאכל לכל אדם, והכהן נוטל דמיו, ולכהן קרי בעלים של בכור. ומעשר — הנאת מכירתו ביוקר לבעליו ישראל היא. ומשום הנאת הדיוטות לא מזלזלינן בקדשים לנהוג בהן מנהג חולין, למוכרו באיטליז, אלא בביתו — ואף על פי שלא יקפצו עליהם בני אדם כל כך — ואין נשקלין בליטרא אלא באומד; ואם יפסיד — לית לן בה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:15:2.english: Their benefit belongs to the owners - [With regard to a] firstborn, its benefit belongs to the priest, and he may sell the meat to whomever he wishes, as the meat of a firstborn may be eaten by any person, and the priest takes its proceeds; and [the Mishnah] calls the priest the "owner" of the firstborn. And [with regard to animal] tithe — the benefit of selling it at a high price belongs to its owner, [who is] an Israelite. And on account of the benefit of private individuals, we do not treat consecrated [animals] with disrespect by treating them in the manner of non-sacred [animals] — to sell it in a butchers’ market, but rather [only] in his house, even though people will not jump at [buying] them as much; and they are not weighed by the litra, but rather by estimate; and if he incurs a loss, we have no concern about it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:16:1.hebrew: ושוקלין מנה כנגד מנה בבכור - שאם יש לו חתיכת בשר חולין שנשקלה בליטרא, יכול לשקול בשר בכור כנגדה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:16:1.english: And one may weigh a portion against a portion in [the case of] a firstborn - For if one has a piece of non-sacred meat that was weighed by the litra, he may weigh firstborn meat against it:

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:1:1.hebrew: וכולן שחזרו בהן - סיפא דהך ברייתא דלעיל היא, דקתני: הבא לקבל דברי חבירות חוץ מדבר אחד, וכן כהן שקיבל עליו דברי כהונה חוץ מדבר אחד, וכן בלוי שקיבל עליו דברי לויה חוץ מדבר אחד — אין מקבלין אותן, שנאמר: המקריב את דם השלמים וגו'. בזמן שהכהנים עושין רצונו של מקום, מה כתיב בהם? חלקם נתתי אותם מאשי. וכשאין עושין רצונו של מקום, מה כתיב בהן? מי גם בכם ויסגור דלתים. וכולן שחזרו בהן אין מקבלין אותם עולמית, כו' — בתוספתא דמסכת דמאי, בפ' האורז במקומו מותר בחלת אנטוכיא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:1:1.english: And all of them, when they retract - [This] is the concluding clause of that baraita from above, which teaches: One who comes to accept the matters of fellowship [ḥaverut] except for one matter, and likewise a priest who accepted upon himself the matters of priesthood except for one matter, and likewise regarding a Levite who accepted upon himself the matters of the levitical office except for one matter — they do not accept them; as it is stated: “He that sacrifices the blood of the peace-offerings...” When the priests perform the will of the Omnipresent, what is written of them? “I have given it to them for their portion of My offerings made by fire”; and when they do not perform the will of the Omnipresent, what is written of them? “Oh that there were even one among you that would shut the doors...”; “and all of them, when they retract, they never accept them,” etc. — in the Tosefta of Tractate Demai, in the chapter [beginning] “Rice in its place is permitted with the dough-offering of Antioch.”

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:2:1.hebrew: עשו דברים במטמוניות - שלא חיללו שם שמים בפרהסיא, מקבלין אותם:
Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:2:1.english: [If] they performed [their] deeds in secret - Since they did not desecrate the Name of Heaven in public, they are accepted.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:3:1.hebrew: כאותו הזוג - ר"ש ור' יהושע בן קרחה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:3:1.english: In accordance with that pair - Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:4:1.english: A collector - One appointed by the king to collect tax from Israelites.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:4:2.english: [If] he withdrew - From tax collection.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:5:1.english: The hour needed him - That the Sages needed him to ask him halakhot.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:5:2.english: He tied for them - He tied and prepared four hundred for them.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:5:4.hebrew: זיל לחשיבותיה - ילך לחשיבותיה, אחר החשיבות שבחר לו להיות מוכס, ואנו לא נלך אצלו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:5:4.english: Go to his importance - Let him go to his importance, following the importance that he chose for himself to be a tax collector, and we will not go to him.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:5:5.english: I have retracted - From tax collection.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:7:1.hebrew: ורואה את קדשיו - אם יש לו שלמים בביתו ונפל בהן מום, יראה אם קבוע הוא, ויפדם ויוציאם לחול:
Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:7:1.english: And he may inspect his sanctified animals - If he has peace offerings in his house and a blemish befell them, he may inspect [them to see] whether it is permanent, and redeem them, and release them to non-sacred status.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:7:2.english: His tithes - Animal tithes in which a blemish developed.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:7:3.hebrew: ונשאל על טהרותיו - הוא עצמו, אם בקי בהלכות, נשאל לעצמו על טהרותיו אם אירע בהן ספק, ואינו צריך לילך אצל חכם אחר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:7:3.english: And is consulted concerning his ritually pure items - He himself, if he is expert in the halakhot, is consulted for himself concerning his ritually pure items if an uncertainty arose regarding them, and he does not need to go to another sage.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:8:1.english: Except for his own - For a priest is not permitted to inspect a blemish on his firstborns and permit it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:8:2.hebrew: וחד מי מהימן - להתיר בכור, ואפילו של אחרים? והאנן תנן לקמן בפרק כל פסולי המוקדשין (בכורות דף לו:): בכור שניסמית עינו ונקטעה ידו — הרי זה ישחט על פי שלשה בני הכנסת:
Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:8:2.english: And is one trusted - To permit a firstborn [to be slaughtered], even [one belonging to] others? But didn't we learn below in the chapter [entitled] Kol Pesulei HaMukdashin (Bekhorot 36b): A firstborn whose eye was blinded or whose foreleg was severed, behold, this [animal] may be slaughtered on the authority of three members of the synagogue [i.e., laymen]?

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:8:3.english: Rather, with three - And the priest, the owner of the firstborn, is one of them.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:8:4.english: And are they suspected - [Would] all of them [be suspected] on his account?

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:8:6.hebrew: מיאנה או שחלצה - אשה לפני החכם, מותר לישאנה, ואינו נחשד לומר: על מנת כן התירה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:8:6.english: She performed refusal or performed ḥalitza - [If] a woman [did so] before the Sage, he is permitted to marry her, and he is not suspected, [such that people would] say: It was with this in mind that he permitted her.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:8:7.hebrew: מפני שהוא ב"ד - כלומר, שלא היה לבדו שם, אלא בית דין שלשה היו שם:
Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:8:7.english: Because he is [part of] a court - That is to say, he was not there alone, but rather a court of three was there.

Rashi on Bekhorot 31a:9:1.english: As Rav Ḥisda said [that] Rabbi Yoḥanan said: By a single expert - In Tractate Nedarim, in the chapter [entitled] Na'arah HaMeorasah (Nedarim 78a).

Tosafot on Bekhorot 31a:12:1.hebrew: דהא חזו ליה בימי טומאתו - תימה: ותרומה טמאה, דלא חזיא ליה — וכי לא יהיה נאמן? וכן בשאר כל איסור והיתר? ובהדיא אמרינן בריש הדר (עירובין ד' סג.): "האי צורבא דרבנן חזי ליה לנפשיה":
Tosafot on Bekhorot 31a:12:1.english: "As they are fit for him in his days of impurity" - [This is] difficult: And [with regard to] impure teruma, which is not fit for him, would he indeed not be believed? And likewise regarding all other [matters of] the forbidden and the permitted? And we explicitly say at the beginning of [the chapter] Hadar (Eruvin 63a): "A Torah scholar may examine [a slaughtering knife] for himself."

Tosafot on Bekhorot 31a:15:1.hebrew: חוץ מן הבכור והמעשר שהנאתן לבעלים - אע"פ שמפרש טעם משום דהנאתן לבעלים, על כרחין מדאורייתא היא — כדמוכח בפרק קמא דתמורה (דף ח.) ובסוף חלק (סנהדרין דף קיב:) גבי עיר הנדחת, דדריש: "בהמתך" — מי שנאכלין בתורת בהמתך, יצא בכור ומעשר שאין נאכלין בתורת בהמתך; דתנן: "כל פסולי המוקדשין נמכרין באיטליז חוץ מן הבכור והמעשר". ושמא משום קרא נפקא, דאין נוהגין בזיון בדבר שאין הנאתן להקדש:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 31a:15:1.english: "Except for the firstborn and the tithe, for their benefit belongs to the owners" - Even though [the Mishnah] explains the reason [as being] because their benefit belongs to the owners, perforce it is from the Torah, as is proven in the first chapter of Temurah (8a) and at the end of [the chapter entitled] Chelek (Sanhedrin 112b) regarding the condemned city, where [the Gemara] expounds: "Your livestock" — that which is eaten in the manner of your livestock; this excludes a firstborn and a tithe, which are not eaten in the manner of your livestock, as we learned in a Mishnah: "All disqualified consecrated animals are sold in the butcher shop, except for the firstborn and the tithe." And perhaps it is derived from Scripture that one does not treat with degradation a matter whose benefit does not belong to the Temple treasury.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 31a:1:1.hebrew: וכולן שחזרו בהן כו' - פ"ה בפ"ק דע"ז (דף ז.): אגזלנים ועמי הארץ קאי, שחזרו מרשען למוטב. וזהו תימה: למה אין מקבלין אותם? דמשמע דאין תקנה לעשות עם הארץ [חבר] שמקבל עליו דברי חבירות, כו'! ועוד, דלשון "עולמית" משמע שכבר קבלו פעם אחרת! ועוד, דאמר רבי יהודה: "חזרו בהן במטמוניות אין מקבלין אותן" — שאם חזרו למוטב במטמוניות ולא בפרהסיא אין מקבלין אותן; וכי זו ירא שמים בסתר?! ואומר ר"ת, דקאי ארישא, דקתני בתוספתא דדמאי בפרק שני: "עם הארץ שקבל עליו דברי חבירות כו' (עובד כוכבים שקבל עליו דברי חבירות כו') גר שקיבל עליו דברי תורה כו' כהן שקבל עליו כהונה כו' לוי שקבל עבודת לויה כו'", והדר קתני: "וכולן שחזרו בהן" — כלומר שחזרו לסורם וקלקלו מעשיהם — "אין מקבלין אותן עולמית", כיון דלא יכלו לעמוד בה. ר' יהודה אומר: "במטמוניות" — כלומר שחזרו לסורם במטמוניות ובגלוי נזהרין על דברי חבירות — אין מקבלין אותן, שגונבין דעת הבריות ואין עושין אלא לפנים; אבל אם לגמרי קלקלו מעשיהם אף בפרהסיא, מקבלין אותן כשישוב, דכשחוזרין חזרה לגמרי:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 31a:1:1.english: "And all of them, when they retract, etc." - Rashi explained in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (7a) that it refers to robbers and amei ha’aretz who repented from their wickedness to good [behavior]. And this is astonishing: Why are they not accepted? For this implies that there is no remedy to make an am ha’aretz a [ḥaver] who accepts upon himself the obligations of ḥaverut, etc.! And furthermore, the expression "never" [olamit] implies that they had already accepted them another time [previously]! And furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda says: "If they retracted in private, they are not accepted" — [meaning, according to Rashi,] that if they repented in private and not in public, they are not accepted; but is this [not being] God-fearing in secret?! And Rabbeinu Tam says that it refers to the beginning [of the passage], as it teaches in the Tosefta of Demai in the second chapter: "An am ha’aretz who accepted upon himself the obligations of ḥaverut, etc.; (an idolater who accepted upon himself the obligations of ḥaverut, etc.); a convert who accepted upon himself the matters of the Torah, etc.; a priest who accepted upon himself the priesthood, etc.; a Levite who accepted the service of the Levites, etc."; and then it teaches: "And all of them, when they retract" — that is to say, they returned to their [corrupt] way and corrupted their deeds — "they are never accepted," since they were unable to abide by it. Rabbi Yehuda says: "In private" — that is to say, if they returned to their [corrupt] way in private, while in public they are careful regarding the obligations of ḥaverut, they are not accepted, because they deceive people and only act for appearances; but if they corrupted their deeds entirely, even in public, they are accepted when they repent, for when they return, it is a complete return.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 31a:2:1.hebrew: איכא דאמרי עשו דבריהם במטמוניות - שהכרנו בהם מתחלה, קודם שחזרו לסורם, שהיו נוהגין דברי חבירות אף בסתר — מקבלין אותם כשישובו. אבל אם לא הכרנו בהם מעולם שעשו דברי חבירות כי אם בפרהסיא, ובצנעה לא היו נזהרין היטב — אין מקבלין אותם, שגונבי דעת הבריות הם:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 31a:2:1.english: "There are those who say: [If] they performed their actions in private" - [This means] that if we recognized in them initially, before they reverted to their corrupt ways, that they observed the practices of ḥaverut even in secret, they are accepted when they return. But if we never recognized in them that they observed the practices of ḥaverut except in public, and in private they were not properly careful, they are not accepted, for they deceive people.
